name: AI sales agent
answer: An AI sales agent is software built on a large language model that handles repeatable sales work: answering buyer questions, qualifying leads, drafting follow-ups and quotes, and updating the CRM. It works through tools such as email, chat and your CRM API, and good setups keep a human approving anything that commits price or terms.
defn: A sales agent sits between your lead sources and your sales team. Instead of a fixed chatbot script, it reads each conversation, decides the next useful step, calls a tool (look up a product, check stock, create a CRM task) and writes a reply or draft in your voice.
does: Reply to inbound enquiries within minutes, around the clock
Ask qualifying questions (budget, timeline, use case) and score the lead
Draft personalised follow-ups after calls, demos or quiet periods
Prepare quotes and price-list answers from approved pricing only
Log activities, notes and next steps to the CRM
Hand hot leads to a human with a short summary of the conversation
data: Past won and lost deal notes
kpis: Median minutes from enquiry to first useful answer
Share of qualified leads that book a call
Percent of open deals with a next step logged
How often reps rewrite the agent's drafts; falling is good
risks: Promising discounts or terms that were never approved
Restrict pricing to a read-only price tool and require human approval on any quote
Contacting people who opted out
Check consent and suppression lists before every send
Hallucinated product facts
Answer only from retrieved product docs and say 'I'll check' otherwise
flow: New enquiry arrives from form, chat or email
Agent enriches the contact from the CRM and classifies intent
Agent answers questions using retrieved product facts
Agent proposes a next step (call, quote, demo) and drafts the message
A rep approves or edits; the agent logs the outcome to the CRM
prompt: You are the sales assistant for {company}. Answer only from the product sheet provided. Qualify the lead on budget, timeline and use case. Never offer a discount. If the lead is ready, propose two meeting slots and draft the email for approval.
memory: Short-term conversation state plus a per-contact summary stored on the CRM record so the next touch knows what was promised.
rag: Index the price list, product pages and objection-handling notes; retrieve the top passages per question and cite them in internal notes.
hitl: Quotes, discounts, contracts and the first message to a new segment are approved by a person.
faqs: Can an AI sales agent close deals on its own?
It can move simple, low-value orders to checkout, but for most businesses it should qualify, follow up and prepare quotes while a person approves pricing and terms.
Which CRM works best with an AI sales agent?
Any CRM with an API works. HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive and Zoho all expose contacts, deals and tasks that an agent can read and update.
How long does it take to build one?
A basic inbound-reply and follow-up agent on n8n or LangGraph takes a few days; CRM write-back, approvals and evaluation usually take two to four weeks.
Will buyers know they are talking to AI?
They should. Disclose that replies are AI-assisted, which is also required in some jurisdictions under consumer protection and AI transparency rules.
evals: Replay 50 real past enquiries and grade the agent's replies for accuracy, tone and correct next step before going live.
job: answers buyer questions, qualifies leads and drafts follow-ups and quotes

name: AI SDR agent
answer: An AI SDR agent automates sales development: it researches target accounts, writes personalised outbound emails or LinkedIn messages, runs follow-up sequences and books meetings for account executives. It relies on enrichment data, a sequencing tool and strict sending limits, and works best when a person reviews messaging and target lists.
defn: SDR stands for sales development representative, the role that turns cold or warm prospects into booked meetings. An AI SDR agent does the research-and-write loop at scale: pick an account, find a reason to reach out, write a short relevant message, and follow up until there is a reply or a clear no.
does: Build target lists from your ideal customer profile
Research each account (news, hiring, tech stack) for a relevant opener
Write first-touch and follow-up messages in a short, plain style
Classify replies (interested, not now, wrong person, unsubscribe)
Book meetings into an AE's calendar
Keep the CRM sequence status accurate
kpis: Interested replies divided by prospects contacted
Deliverability health; keep complaints very low
Spot-check rate of factually correct personalisation
risks: Damaging sender reputation with volume
Cap daily sends per mailbox, warm domains and stop on bounces
Breaking anti-spam and privacy laws
Respect CAN-SPAM, GDPR legitimate-interest rules and opt-outs; include a clear unsubscribe
Creepy or wrong personalisation
Use only public business facts and have a human sample messages weekly
flow: Pull accounts that match the ICP
Research and summarise one relevant trigger per account
Draft a 60-90 word first message and two follow-ups
Human approves the batch or the template
Send on schedule, classify replies and book meetings
prompt: Write a first email under 80 words to {name}, {title} at {company}. Mention {trigger} in one sentence, connect it to {value prop}, and end with a soft question. No flattery, no fake familiarity.
memory: A per-prospect record of touches, replies and the trigger used, so follow-ups reference earlier messages correctly.
rag: Retrieve the most relevant case study and proof point for the prospect's industry and size before drafting.
hitl: New templates, new segments and any reply that mentions pricing, legal or a complaint go to a person.
faqs: Is an AI SDR better than a human SDR?
It is faster at research and volume, but humans still win on judgement, live calls and complex accounts. Most teams use the agent to prepare and send while people handle conversations.
Does AI outbound email still work?
It works when lists are tight and messages are genuinely relevant. Generic AI emails at high volume tend to hurt deliverability and reply rates.
What data does an AI SDR need?
A clear ICP, enrichment data, proof points and reply history. Without good targeting, better writing does not help much.
How do I stay compliant?
Follow CAN-SPAM, GDPR and local rules, honour opt-outs immediately, identify your company and avoid scraping personal data you have no basis to use.
evals: Have two reps blind-rate 30 agent emails against 30 human emails for relevance and accuracy before scaling.
job: researches target accounts, writes personalised outreach and books meetings

name: AI lead qualification agent
answer: An AI lead qualification agent reviews every new lead, asks or infers qualifying details such as budget, authority, need and timeline, scores the lead, and routes it to the right person or nurture track. It reduces time wasted on poor-fit leads and makes sure good ones are contacted fast.
defn: Qualification is the filter between marketing and sales. An AI agent applies your criteria consistently, uses forms, chat answers and enrichment data, and explains why it gave each score so sales can trust it.
does: Read form fills, chat transcripts and emails as they arrive
Enrich company size, industry and location
Ask missing questions politely by chat or email
Score against BANT, MEDDIC or your own criteria
Route to the right rep, territory or nurture sequence
Write a two-line summary on the CRM record
kpis: Minutes from lead creation to owner assigned
Agreement between agent score and rep judgement
How many routed leads become real deals
Good leads scored low; should trend to zero
risks: Biased or unfair scoring
Score on business criteria only, never on protected traits, and audit samples
Over-asking and annoying buyers
Limit to two or three questions and skip what enrichment already knows
Silent routing failures
Alert a human when a lead sits unassigned beyond a threshold
flow: Lead created in CRM or form tool
Agent enriches and checks for duplicates
Agent asks one to three missing questions if needed
Agent scores with reasons and picks a route
Owner is alerted with a summary; low-fit leads go to nurture
prompt: Score this lead 0-100 against our rubric. Return JSON with score, route (sales, nurture, disqualify) and a one-sentence reason. If budget or timeline is unknown, write one short question to ask.
memory: Lead-level notes and score history on the CRM record; no long-term memory beyond that is needed.
rag: Retrieve the scoring rubric and similar past leads with known outcomes to calibrate the score.
hitl: Disqualifications of large accounts and any lead that mentions an existing customer issue go to a person.
faqs: What is the difference between lead scoring and AI lead qualification?
Classic scoring adds points for fixed actions. An AI agent also reads free text, asks follow-up questions and explains its decision.
Which framework should the agent use: BANT or MEDDIC?
BANT suits smaller deals; MEDDIC suits complex B2B sales. The agent can apply either as long as the rubric is written down.
Can it qualify leads on WhatsApp?
Yes, through the WhatsApp Business API, using approved templates for the first outbound message.
How do I know the scores are right?
Compare agent scores with rep outcomes monthly and adjust the rubric or examples where they disagree.
evals: Back-test the rubric on 200 historical leads and check how many eventual customers it would have routed to sales.
job: scores new leads against your criteria and routes them to the right person

name: AI customer support agent
answer: An AI customer support agent answers customer questions across chat, email and messaging apps using your help articles, order data and policies. It resolves routine requests such as order status, returns and how-to questions, and hands complex or sensitive cases to a human with full context, so customers get faster answers without losing the option to reach a person.
defn: Support agents combine retrieval (finding the right help article or policy) with actions (looking up an order, starting a return). The difference from an old chatbot is that the agent understands free-form questions and can take several steps to resolve them.
does: Answer FAQs and how-to questions from the knowledge base
Look up order, booking or account status
Start returns, refunds or exchanges within policy limits
Collect details and create a ticket when it cannot resolve
Detect frustration or urgent issues and escalate
Draft replies for agents in the help desk
kpis: Conversations fully solved without a human
Seconds or minutes to the first useful reply
Share of handoffs with complete context
risks: Making up policy or refund promises
Answer only from retrieved policy text and cap refund actions by amount
Trapping customers in a bot loop
Offer a human route at any time and after two failed attempts
Exposing personal data
Verify identity before account actions and redact sensitive fields in logs
flow: Customer message arrives on any channel
Agent identifies intent and the customer record
Agent retrieves policy or article and checks order data
Agent resolves or takes an allowed action
If unresolved or sensitive, it creates a ticket with a summary for a human
prompt: You are {company}'s support assistant. Use only the articles and order data provided. If the answer is not there, say you will pass it to the team. Offer a human at any point. Never promise a refund above {limit}.
memory: Conversation history within the ticket plus customer profile; past tickets are retrieved on demand rather than kept in the prompt.
rag: Chunk help articles and policies by heading, embed them, and retrieve with the customer's question plus product context.
hitl: Refunds above a limit, legal threats, safety issues and VIP customers go to a person.
faqs: What share of support tickets can an AI agent resolve?

It depends on how routine your tickets are and how good your help content is. Order status, returns and how-to questions are the easiest to automate; billing disputes and complaints usually need people.
Does an AI support agent replace the support team?
Usually not. It takes the repetitive volume so people can focus on complex, emotional or high-value cases.
How do I train it on my business?
Give it your help articles, policies and a sample of resolved tickets, then test on real past questions before launch.
Can it work on WhatsApp and Instagram?
Yes, through the official business APIs for each channel, connected to the same knowledge base.
evals: Run the agent against 100 resolved tickets and score answer correctness, policy compliance and tone; launch only above your quality bar.
job: answers customer questions from your policies and data and hands complex cases to staff

name: AI ticket triage agent
answer: An AI ticket triage agent reads each incoming support or service ticket, classifies its topic, urgency and sentiment, detects duplicates, fills missing fields and routes it to the right queue or person. It shortens time to first response and keeps queues clean without answering customers itself.
defn: Triage is the sorting step before resolution. Many teams start with triage because it is low risk: the agent only labels and routes, and humans still reply.
does: Classify topic, product area and language
Set priority from urgency cues and customer tier
Detect duplicates and link related tickets
Extract order numbers, device models or account IDs
Route to the correct queue, team or specialist
Suggest a macro or relevant article to the human agent
tools: Help desk or ITSM (Zendesk, Jira Service Management, ServiceNow, Freshservice)
kpis: Tickets that land in the right queue first time
Tickets that miss their response target
How often tickets bounce between teams
risks: Mislabelling urgent issues as low priority
Use conservative rules for keywords like outage, legal, safety and always escalate them
Taxonomy drift
Review confusion between labels monthly and update examples
Privacy of ticket content
Process data in your own cloud region and restrict logs
flow: Ticket created by email, form or chat
Agent extracts fields and classifies topic, priority and sentiment
Agent checks for duplicates and active incidents
Agent assigns queue and suggests a macro
Human resolves; corrections feed the next evaluation set
prompt: Classify this ticket. Return JSON: topic (from list), priority (P1-P4), sentiment, language, duplicate_of (if any), suggested_macro. Mark P1 if it mentions outage, data loss, safety or legal action.
memory: No long-term memory needed; each ticket is classified with its thread and customer tier.
rag: Retrieve similar past tickets with their final labels as few-shot examples.
hitl: Humans resolve every ticket; the agent only labels and routes. Low-confidence labels are flagged.
faqs: Is AI triage safer than an AI agent that replies?
Yes. Because it only labels and routes, mistakes cost time rather than customer trust, which makes it a good first project.
How accurate does triage need to be?
Aim for accuracy at least as good as your current manual routing, with urgent categories tuned for recall over precision.
Can a small model do triage?
Often yes. Classification is a narrow task, and a small or fine-tuned model can be fast and cheap.
Does it work with Jira or ServiceNow?
Yes, both expose APIs and webhooks for reading tickets and updating fields.
evals: Hold out 300 labelled tickets and measure per-label precision and recall, especially for P1 and legal categories.
job: classifies, prioritises and routes incoming tickets without replying itself

name: AI voice receptionist agent
answer: An AI voice receptionist agent answers phone calls with natural speech, handles common questions, books or changes appointments, takes messages and transfers callers to staff when needed. It combines speech-to-text, a language model and text-to-speech with calendar and CRM tools, so calls are answered even after hours or during busy periods.
defn: Voice agents work in real time, so latency and interruptions matter more than in chat. A typical stack streams the caller's audio to a speech recogniser, sends text to the model with tools, and streams the reply back as synthetic speech in under a second.
does: Answer every call, including after hours
Answer hours, location, pricing and service questions
Book, reschedule or cancel appointments
Take detailed messages and send them by SMS or email
Transfer urgent or complex calls to a person
Log call summaries in the CRM
kpis: Calls that end with an appointment
Response delay per turn; keep it near conversational speed
Calls passed to staff and why
risks: Recording consent and disclosure
Announce the AI assistant and recording where the law requires it
Wrong bookings
Confirm date and time back to the caller and send an SMS confirmation
Emergency calls
Detect emergencies and give emergency guidance or transfer immediately
flow: Call connects and the agent greets with disclosure
Speech is transcribed and intent detected
Agent answers or checks the calendar via tools
Agent confirms details aloud and books
Summary and recording link are saved; urgent calls are transferred
prompt: You are the receptionist for {business}. Speak in short sentences. Confirm names, dates and times back to the caller. If the caller mentions an emergency, tell them to call local emergency services and transfer to staff.
memory: Per-call state plus caller lookup by phone number for returning customers.
rag: Retrieve service, pricing and policy snippets; keep the knowledge base short so lookups stay fast.
hitl: Transfers for complaints, emergencies and anything outside the booking rules; staff review summaries daily.
faqs: Do callers accept talking to an AI receptionist?
Most accept it for simple tasks when the agent is fast, clear and offers a human. Disclose that it is an AI assistant.
What latency is acceptable for a voice agent?
Replies that start within about a second feel conversational; longer pauses cause callers to talk over the agent.
Can it speak more than one language?
Yes, most modern speech models handle several languages, but test accents and names in each one.
What does it cost to run?
Costs are usually per minute and combine telephony, speech recognition, the language model and speech synthesis.
evals: Run 50 scripted test calls covering bookings, edge cases, accents and emergencies before taking live calls.
oursNote: AI Time Machine does not answer phone calls. Its Support agents draft written replies (chat, email, WhatsApp) that you approve.
job: answers phone calls, handles common questions and books appointments

name: AI marketing agent
answer: An AI marketing agent plans, drafts and monitors marketing work: campaign ideas, ad copy, audience suggestions, landing-page text and weekly performance summaries. It connects to ad platforms, analytics and content tools, and it should propose changes for a marketer to approve rather than spend budget on its own.
defn: Marketing agents are usually a small team of specialised steps rather than one prompt: a planner that sets the goal, writers that produce variants, and an analyst that reads results and suggests the next test.
does: Turn a goal into a campaign plan with channels and timeline
Write ad headlines, descriptions and offer angles
Suggest audiences and keywords to test
Summarise weekly results from ads and analytics
Flag wasted spend or broken tracking
Prepare festival or seasonal campaign calendars
tools: Google Ads and Meta Ads APIs
kpis: Revenue per unit of ad spend
Share of agent drafts approved without major edits
risks: Spending budget without oversight
Give the agent read-only ad access or require approval for budget changes
Misleading claims in ads
Check copy against advertising rules and a list of approved claims
Optimising to fake conversions
Verify conversion tracking counts real purchases before optimising
flow: Marketer sets a goal and budget
Planner agent drafts a channel plan
Writer agent creates copy variants on brand
Marketer approves; ads are launched by a person or with approval
Analyst agent reports weekly and proposes the next test
prompt: Plan a two-week campaign for {product} aimed at {audience} with a budget of {budget}. Give three angles, five headlines per angle under 30 characters, and the metric to judge each. Use only claims from the approved list.
memory: Campaign history and test results stored in a table the agent reads at the start of each planning cycle.
rag: Retrieve brand guidelines, approved claims and the best past ads for the same audience.
hitl: Budgets, new claims, audiences with sensitive targeting and anything published goes through a person.
faqs: Can an AI marketing agent run my ads automatically?
It can, but most businesses should let it draft and recommend while a person approves budget and launches, at least until the tracking and guardrails are proven.
What tools does it need access to?
Usually ad platforms, analytics, your brand guide and a place to store results. Read-only access is a safe start.
Is AI ad copy allowed on Google and Meta?
Yes, but the same ad policies apply. You are responsible for claims, so review copy before it runs.
How is it different from a content agent?
A marketing agent plans and measures campaigns; a content agent focuses on producing posts, articles and assets.
evals: Compare agent-written ad variants against your current best ads in a small controlled test before scaling spend.
job: plans campaigns, drafts ad and email copy and summarises results

name: AI social media agent
answer: An AI social media agent drafts posts, captions, Reels and Shorts ideas, schedules content, and helps reply to comments and messages in your brand voice. It connects to scheduling tools and platform APIs, keeps a content calendar, and leaves publishing and sensitive replies for a person to approve.
defn: Social agents mostly do volume writing and organisation: turning one idea into platform-specific versions, keeping a calendar full, and sorting comments into ones it can answer and ones a person should see.
does: Generate a weekly content calendar from themes and events
Write captions and hashtags per platform
Turn a blog post or video into several social posts
Suggest Reels or Shorts hooks and scripts
Draft replies to comments and DMs
Summarise engagement and best-performing formats
tools: Scheduling tool (Buffer, Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Metricool)
Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X and TikTok APIs
kpis: Planned posts actually published per week
Median time to respond to questions
Traffic from social to site with UTM tags
risks: Off-brand or insensitive posts
Keep a banned-topics list and require approval before publishing
Copyright issues in images or music
Use licensed assets and your own media
Platform policy violations
Follow each platform's automation rules and API terms
flow: Agent proposes weekly themes from calendar and goals
Agent drafts posts per platform with asset suggestions
Person approves and schedules
Agent drafts comment replies for review
Weekly summary shows what to repeat
prompt: Write five Instagram captions for {product} in our voice: friendly, short, no more than two emojis. Each needs a hook in the first line and a clear call to action. Add 5 relevant hashtags.
memory: Calendar and post history so the agent avoids repeating hooks and topics.
rag: Retrieve brand voice examples and top-performing past posts as style references.
hitl: Every publish and every reply to complaints, press or sensitive topics is approved by a person.
faqs: Can an AI agent post to Instagram automatically?
Yes, through the Instagram Graph API for business accounts, but approving each post first avoids brand mistakes.
Will AI-written posts hurt reach?
Platforms rank on engagement, not authorship. Generic posts underperform; specific, useful ones do fine.
Can it make videos too?
It can write scripts and hooks, and some tools generate video, but filming real people and products still performs best.
How do I keep the brand voice consistent?
Give it a short voice guide with examples of good and bad posts, and correct drafts so examples improve.
evals: Have the agent draft a month of posts from past briefs and compare approval rate and engagement against human posts.
job: drafts posts and replies, keeps a content calendar and reports engagement

name: AI SEO agent
answer: An AI SEO agent researches keywords and questions, audits pages for technical and on-page issues, drafts optimised titles, descriptions and content briefs, and tracks rankings and Search Console data. It speeds up routine SEO work, but its suggestions should be reviewed so content stays accurate, original and genuinely helpful.
defn: SEO agents work across three loops: research (what people search), production (briefs, titles, schema), and monitoring (crawl errors, rankings, click-through rates). They are most useful on repetitive, data-heavy tasks.
does: Find keywords and real questions people ask
Cluster keywords into topics and page plans
Audit titles, meta descriptions, headings and internal links
Draft content briefs and FAQ sections
Generate structured data (JSON-LD)
Monitor Search Console for drops and errors
kpis: Search Console clicks to target pages
Valid pages in the index versus submitted
Clicks divided by impressions for target queries
risks: Thin or duplicate AI content
Publish only pages with original substance and real expertise; follow Google's helpful content guidance
Wrong technical changes
Test changes on staging and review robots, canonical and redirect edits
Keyword stuffing
Write for readers first and check readability
flow: Agent pulls queries and crawl data
Agent clusters topics and finds gaps
Agent drafts briefs, titles and schema
Editor reviews and publishes
Agent monitors results and flags drops
prompt: Given these Search Console queries for /pricing, suggest a title under 60 characters and a meta description under 155 characters that match intent. Do not invent features.
memory: A table of pages, target queries and past changes, so the agent can link changes to results.
rag: Retrieve the page's current content and the top-ranking competitor outlines for the query.
hitl: Publishing, redirects, robots and canonical changes require a person.
faqs: Does Google penalise AI-written content?
Google evaluates helpfulness and quality, not whether AI was used. Mass-produced pages without original value can be treated as scaled content abuse.
Can an AI SEO agent fix technical issues?
It can find and explain them and draft fixes, but changes to robots, canonicals and redirects should be reviewed.
What is AEO or GEO?
Answer engine and generative engine optimisation: structuring content so AI assistants and AI search can quote it accurately.
Which data source matters most?
Search Console, because it shows the queries and pages Google actually associates with your site.
evals: Track a set of target pages for eight weeks after agent-suggested changes against an untouched control set.
job: researches search demand, audits pages and drafts titles, briefs and schema

name: AI content writing agent
answer: An AI content writing agent researches a topic, outlines, drafts and edits articles, product descriptions, newsletters and landing pages in your brand voice. Strong setups add fact-checking against sources, an editorial checklist and human review, because publishing unverified AI text risks errors and weak search performance.
defn: Content agents chain steps: research, outline, draft, critique and revise. Splitting the work this way produces better results than asking one prompt for a finished article.
does: Research a topic and collect sources
Create outlines that match search intent
Draft articles, emails and product descriptions
Rewrite for tone, length and reading level
Check facts and add citations
Repurpose long content into short formats
kpis: Hours from brief to editable draft
How much editors change; falling means better drafts
Errors found per article in review
Time on page, scroll depth and conversions
risks: Fabricated facts or quotes
Require a source for each claim and verify before publishing
Plagiarism
Run originality checks and avoid copying competitor text
Same-sounding content
Feed real examples, data and expert input into each piece
flow: Brief with audience, intent and sources
Research and outline step
Draft step in brand voice
Critique step checks facts, structure and style
Editor reviews and publishes
prompt: Draft a 1,200-word article for {audience} on {topic}. Use only facts from the attached sources and cite them inline. Include a short summary at the top and three FAQs. Flag any claim you could not verify.
memory: Style guide and list of published articles so the agent avoids repeating angles and adds internal links.
rag: Retrieve source documents and past articles for facts and internal-link candidates.
hitl: An editor reviews every piece before publishing, especially claims, numbers and quotes.
faqs: Is AI-written content good enough to publish?
Drafts can be good, but publishing without editing risks factual errors and generic writing. Treat the agent as a fast first-draft writer.
How do I keep the brand voice?
Provide a style guide and several annotated examples, and use a critique step that checks against them.
Can it write in other languages?
Yes, but have a native speaker review important content.
Do I have to disclose AI use?
Rules vary. Being transparent with readers is good practice, and some platforms and regions require it.
evals: Have editors score ten drafts on accuracy, structure and voice against a checklist before using the agent in production.
job: researches, drafts and edits articles and copy with sources

name: AI email marketing agent
answer: An AI email marketing agent writes campaigns and automated flows, segments subscribers, suggests send times and subject lines, and summarises results. It works with platforms such as Klaviyo or Mailchimp, and it must respect consent, unsubscribe rules and brand review before anything is sent.
defn: Email agents focus on lifecycle messages: welcome series, abandoned cart, win-back and newsletters. Their value is producing personalised variants and keeping flows up to date without a large team.
does: Draft newsletters and promotional campaigns
Write automated flows (welcome, cart, win-back)
Suggest segments from behaviour and purchase data
Create subject-line and preview-text variants for testing
Summarise opens, clicks and revenue by campaign
Flag deliverability problems
tools: WhatsApp or SMS for multi-channel flows
kpis: Attributed revenue divided by emails delivered
Key lifecycle stages with a live flow
risks: Sending without consent
Only email opted-in contacts and honour unsubscribes immediately
Over-sending and list fatigue
Set frequency caps per subscriber
Wrong personalisation tokens
Test with sample profiles before every send
flow: Goal and segment chosen
Agent drafts copy, subject lines and layout notes
Marketer approves and the agent builds in the platform as draft
Test send to internal list
Scheduled send and results summary
prompt: Write a three-email win-back flow for customers who have not bought in 90 days. Friendly tone, no fake urgency. Email 1 is a reminder, email 2 shares a helpful tip, email 3 offers {offer}. Give two subject lines per email.
memory: Campaign calendar and test results so the agent avoids repeating offers and builds on winning subject lines.
rag: Retrieve product data, past high-performing emails and brand rules for each draft.
hitl: Every campaign send and any change to automated flows is approved by a person.
faqs: Can AI write my email newsletters?
Yes. It produces solid drafts quickly; add your own news, data and opinions so it does not read generic.
Will AI emails land in spam?
Spam filtering depends on sender reputation, authentication and engagement, not on whether AI wrote the copy.
Can it personalise for each subscriber?
Yes, using purchase and behaviour data, within privacy rules and consent.
What about WhatsApp marketing?
Many agents also draft WhatsApp broadcasts, which need opt-in and approved templates.
evals: A/B test agent-written subject lines and bodies against your current best on a small segment first.
job: writes campaigns and automated flows and suggests segments

name: AI review response agent
answer: An AI review response agent monitors reviews on Google, marketplaces and app stores, drafts personal replies in your voice, flags urgent complaints and summarises recurring themes. It helps businesses reply to every review quickly while a person approves replies to negative or sensitive reviews.
defn: Reviews influence local search and buying decisions. Replying consistently is time-consuming, so an agent that drafts specific, polite replies and surfaces patterns is one of the most practical small-business agents.
does: Collect new reviews from each platform
Draft replies that mention specifics from the review
Flag angry, legal or safety-related reviews
Suggest service recovery steps for complaints
Ask happy customers for reviews at the right moment
Summarise themes monthly
tools: Marketplace and app store review APIs
kpis: Share of reviews with a reply
Negative reviewers who were contacted and resolved
risks: Defensive or argumentative replies
Use a calm template for negative reviews and require approval
Fake review solicitation
Never offer incentives for positive reviews; follow platform rules and consumer law
Disclosing private details
Never confirm health, booking or account details in a public reply
flow: New review detected
Agent classifies sentiment and topic
Agent drafts a specific reply
Person approves negative or sensitive replies; positive ones can auto-post if allowed
Monthly theme summary goes to the owner
prompt: Draft a reply to this 2-star review. Thank them, acknowledge the specific issue, avoid excuses, and invite them to contact {email}. Under 70 words. Do not mention any personal details.
memory: Reviewer history and past replies so repeat reviewers get a consistent response.
rag: Retrieve the service recovery policy and similar past reviews with approved replies.
hitl: Replies to 1-3 star reviews and anything legal, medical or safety-related are approved by a person.
faqs: Should I reply to every review?
Replying to most reviews, especially negative ones, shows customers you listen. An agent makes it practical.
Can AI replies sound personal?
Yes, if the agent references specific details from each review and avoids repeating the same phrases.
Is it allowed to auto-post replies?
Platforms allow owner replies through official tools and APIs; check each platform's policy.
Can it ask customers for reviews?
It can draft requests, but do not offer rewards for positive reviews or filter who gets asked based on sentiment.
evals: Review 40 agent drafts across star ratings for tone, specificity and policy before turning on auto-posting for positive reviews.
job: monitors reviews, drafts replies and flags urgent complaints

name: AI recruiting agent
answer: An AI recruiting agent helps hiring teams source candidates, screen applications against job requirements, answer candidate questions, schedule interviews and keep the applicant tracking system updated. Because hiring decisions are regulated in many places, it should support recruiters with transparent, auditable recommendations rather than reject people automatically.
defn: Recruiting agents automate the administrative load around hiring: writing job posts, reading CVs, chasing scheduling and keeping candidates informed, so recruiters spend more time talking to people.
does: Draft inclusive job descriptions
Source candidates from approved databases and referrals
Summarise CVs against must-have and nice-to-have criteria

faqs: Is it legal to use AI to screen candidates?
Often yes, with conditions. Some jurisdictions require bias audits, notices or human review, and the EU AI Act treats recruitment AI as high-risk. Get legal advice for your region.
Can an AI recruiter reject candidates automatically?
It should not. Use it to summarise and organise, and keep people responsible for decisions.
Does it help with interview scheduling?
Yes, scheduling is one of the clearest wins because it is repetitive and rule-based.
How do I reduce bias?
Use structured criteria, remove protected attributes from inputs, audit outcomes by group and review samples regularly.

Store ID and bank documents only in the HRIS, never in chat logs
Over-provisioning access
Use role-based templates and manager approval for access
flow: Offer accepted in ATS
Agent builds the plan from role template
Agent requests accounts, equipment and documents
New hire chats with the agent for questions
Agent tracks progress and nudges owners
prompt: You help new employees at {company}. Answer only from the handbook passages provided and include the section name. For pay, visas, medical or disciplinary topics, direct the person to HR.

hitl: Access approvals, contract changes and sensitive HR questions go to people.
faqs: What onboarding tasks can AI automate?
Reminders, document collection, account requests, scheduling and answering common policy questions.
Is it safe to give an agent HR data?
Limit it to what each task needs, keep data in your HR systems, and log access.
Can it replace an HR onboarding coordinator?
It reduces repetitive work; people still handle welcome, culture and sensitive issues.
Does it work for remote employees?

name: AI invoice processing agent
answer: An AI invoice processing agent captures supplier invoices from email or uploads, extracts fields such as supplier, amounts, tax and line items, matches them to purchase orders and receipts, codes them to the right accounts and routes exceptions for approval. It cuts manual data entry in accounts payable while finance approves payments.
defn: Invoice agents combine document AI (OCR plus a language model that understands layouts) with rules from your accounting system. The goal is touchless processing for clean invoices and clear explanations for the rest.
does: Collect invoices from a shared inbox or upload
Extract header fields, tax amounts and line items
Validate supplier, bank details and duplicates
Match to purchase orders and goods receipts
Suggest general ledger codes and cost centres
Route exceptions with a plain explanation
tools: Accounting or ERP (Xero, QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Tally)
kpis: Invoices posted with no manual edits
Total AP cost divided by invoices processed
risks: Paying fraudulent invoices or changed bank details
Verify bank changes out of band and never let the agent release payments
Extraction errors on totals or tax
Cross-check line sums and tax maths and flag mismatches
Wrong account coding
Learn from past coding and require approval for new suppliers
flow: Invoice arrives by email or upload
Agent extracts and validates fields
Agent matches PO and receipt and checks duplicates
Agent proposes coding and approver
Approver approves; agent posts the bill to the accounting system
prompt: Extract supplier name, invoice number, date, currency, subtotal, tax, total and line items as JSON. Check that line items sum to the subtotal and subtotal plus tax equals total. If not, set needs_review to true with the reason.
memory: Supplier profiles with usual coding and amounts to detect anomalies.
rag: Retrieve the supplier record, matching PO and the last three invoices from that supplier.
hitl: Payment release, bank detail changes, new suppliers and all exceptions are approved by finance.
faqs: How accurate is AI invoice extraction?
Modern document AI is very accurate on typed invoices, but always validate totals and tax maths automatically and review exceptions.
Can it handle invoices in different formats and languages?
Yes, layout-aware models handle varied templates and many languages; test on your real suppliers.
Does it work with Tally, Xero or QuickBooks?
Most accounting systems accept bills through an API or import file the agent can produce.
Should the agent pay invoices?
No. Keep payment approval and release with people, especially for new suppliers or changed bank details.

job: extracts, validates and codes supplier invoices and routes exceptions

name: AI bookkeeping agent
answer: An AI bookkeeping agent categorises bank and card transactions, reconciles accounts, matches receipts, prepares month-end summaries and flags unusual items for an accountant. It keeps books current with less manual work, while a qualified person reviews entries, tax treatment and filings.
defn: Bookkeeping is rule-heavy and repetitive, which suits agents. The agent applies your categorisation rules, learns from corrections and writes plain-language explanations of anything that does not fit.
does: Categorise transactions to the chart of accounts
Match receipts and invoices to bank lines
Reconcile bank, card and payment-gateway accounts
Flag duplicates, missing receipts and anomalies
Prepare monthly profit and cash summaries
Remind owners of tax and filing dates
tools: Accounting software (Xero, QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Tally)
kpis: Business day when month-end close finishes
risks: Wrong tax treatment
Have an accountant review tax codes and filings
Hiding errors behind confident summaries
Show the source transactions behind every number
Bank data security
Use read-only bank connections and strong access controls
flow: Transactions sync from bank and gateways
Agent categorises and matches receipts
Agent reconciles and lists exceptions

Agent prepares the month-end summary

memory: Payee-to-category mappings learned from approved corrections.
rag: Retrieve similar past transactions and the categorisation rules.
hitl: An accountant approves exceptions, journal entries and anything tax-related.
faqs: Can AI do my bookkeeping completely?
It can do most categorisation and matching, but a person should review exceptions and tax decisions.
Is AI bookkeeping accurate?
Accuracy improves with clean rules and corrections. Track the edit rate and review low-confidence items.
Does it file my taxes?
It can prepare figures and reminders; filing should be done or reviewed by a qualified professional.
Which accounting software works best?
Any with a good API and bank feeds, such as Xero, QuickBooks or Zoho Books.

name: AI collections agent
answer: An AI collections agent tracks unpaid invoices, sends polite, well-timed payment reminders, answers billing questions, records promises to pay and escalates overdue accounts to a person. It improves cash flow and reduces awkward manual chasing, while staying within debt-collection and consumer-protection rules.
defn: Accounts receivable work is mostly follow-up: knowing who owes what, reminding them at the right time and resolving disputes quickly. An agent handles the routine cadence and keeps every interaction logged.
does: Monitor ageing reports daily
Send reminder sequences by email, SMS or WhatsApp
Share payment links and invoice copies
Answer questions about amounts and due dates
Record promises to pay and disputes
Escalate long-overdue or disputed accounts
risks: Harassment or unfair collection practices
Follow laws such as the U.S. FDCPA for consumer debt, limit frequency and keep tone respectful
Wrong amounts in reminders
Pull live balances before each message
Damaging key relationships
Let account owners pause reminders for strategic customers
flow: Invoice approaches due date
Agent sends a friendly reminder with payment link
Agent answers replies and records promises or disputes
Overdue accounts move through a firmer sequence
Person handles escalations and write-off decisions
prompt: Write a polite reminder for invoice {number} of {amount}, {days} days overdue. Include the payment link. No threats. If they reply with a dispute, stop the sequence and create a ticket.
memory: Customer-level interaction history and promise dates.
rag: Retrieve invoice details, terms and previous correspondence.
hitl: Payment plans, settlements, write-offs and disputes are handled by a person.
faqs: Is it okay to use AI for payment reminders?
Yes, with clear, respectful messages and compliance with collection laws in your region.
Will it hurt customer relationships?
Polite, accurate, well-timed reminders usually help; let account owners exclude sensitive customers.
Can it negotiate payment plans?
It can collect information and propose standard options, but a person should approve plans and settlements.

Email for B2B, plus SMS or WhatsApp where customers have opted in.

name: AI expense audit agent
answer: An AI expense audit agent reviews employee expense claims and card spend against policy, checks receipts, detects duplicates and unusual patterns, and flags claims that need a closer look. It lets finance review every expense instead of a small sample, while people make the final call on rejections.
defn: Traditional expense audits sample a few claims. An agent reads every receipt, compares it with policy and transaction data, and explains each flag so reviewers can act quickly.
does: Read receipts and match them to card transactions
Check amounts, categories and limits against policy
Detect duplicates and split transactions
Spot out-of-policy merchants or weekend spend
Ask employees for missing details
Summarise spend trends by team
tools: Expense tool (Expensify, SAP Concur, Ramp, Brex)
risks: Unfair accusations from false flags
Phrase flags as questions and let people review before action
Privacy of employee spending
Limit access to finance and the employee's manager
Policy ambiguity
Keep a clear written policy and update rules when exceptions are approved

Agent checks policy rules and patterns

Duplicates, missing receipts, out-of-policy spend, mismatched amounts and unusual patterns.

It should flag and explain; final decisions belong to finance or managers.

name: AI data analyst agent
answer: An AI data analyst agent answers business questions in plain language by writing and running SQL or Python against your data, building charts and explaining the results. defn: Analyst agents translate a question like 'why did sales drop last week?' into queries, run them, check the output, and write a short explanation with a chart. The key design choices are data access, a semantic layer that defines metrics, and verification.
does: Translate questions into SQL or Python

Explain trends, drivers and anomalies
Schedule recurring reports and summaries
Document metric definitions
kpis: Minutes from question to verified answer
Questions answered without the data team
risks: Confidently wrong numbers
Show the query, row counts and definitions with every answer
Data leakage
Use read-only roles and row-level security
Runaway query costs
Set limits on bytes scanned and timeouts

Agent looks up metric definitions and schemas
Agent writes and runs a query in a sandbox
Agent checks results for sanity and builds a chart
Agent answers with the query attached

memory: A library of verified queries and definitions the agent reuses.
rag: Retrieve table schemas, column descriptions and verified example queries.
hitl: Numbers used in board, investor or financial reporting are reviewed by an analyst.
faqs: Can AI replace a data analyst?
It handles routine questions and first drafts; analysts still define metrics, check logic and frame decisions.
How do I stop it giving wrong numbers?
Use a semantic layer, show queries, test on known answers and restrict it to governed tables.

Yes, many agents can read spreadsheets or run Python on uploaded files.

name: AI research agent
answer: An AI research agent searches the web, documents and databases, reads sources, and writes structured summaries or reports with citations. It is used for market research, competitor tracking, due diligence and literature reviews, and its output should always be checked against the cited sources.
defn: Research agents run a loop: plan sub-questions, search, read, take notes, and synthesise. Deep-research tools from major model providers follow this pattern, and open-source versions can be built with a few tools.

Search the web and internal documents
Read and extract key facts with sources
Compare competitors, products or vendors
Write briefs with citations
Monitor topics and send updates
kpis: Claims that match their cited source
Relevant sources found versus an expert list
risks: Fabricated or misattributed citations
Verify each citation link and quote automatically and by spot-check
Low-quality sources
Prefer primary and authoritative sources and rank by trust
Copyright and terms of use
Respect robots rules and site terms; quote briefly and link
flow: Brief defines the question and scope
Agent plans sub-questions
Agent searches and reads sources
Agent drafts a cited report
Reviewer checks key claims and sources

memory: Notes store of facts with sources, reused across related questions.

They are fast at finding and summarising sources but can misread or miscite. Check important claims against the sources.

Only sources you have rights to; connect your licensed databases rather than bypassing paywalls.
What is the difference from a search engine?
A search engine returns links; a research agent reads them and writes a structured answer with citations.

Yes. A search API, a scraper and a framework like LangGraph or smolagents are enough for a first version.
